We review every complete application personally and will respond fast to the strong ones.



Thanks for your interest!



Will & David

title: INBOUND APPOINTMENT SETTER — HAIR SALON (WARM FACEBOOK/INSTAGRAM LEADS, $1,250–$2,000/MO OTE + 13TH MONTH PAY)
description:
READ THIS FIRST



We're hiring ONE full-time Inbound Appointment Setter to call warm leads from our
 and Instagram ad campaigns for a color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California.



This is NOT cold calling. Every lead you speak to has already raised their hand by submitting their info through one of our ads. Your job is to reach them fast, build trust quickly, understand what they actually want, and guide them into a booked appointment.



This role demands two things at once: sharp conversational judgment AND tight process discipline. The conversations are where you win or lose the booking. The process — cadences, call dispositions, CRM hygiene, follow-up tasks — is what makes the whole system work and what lets us measure anything. You need both. People who are great at one and sloppy at the other don't last here.



On the conversation side, what we're really hiring for is the ability to think on your feet. Someone replies three days later with just "sorry, been busy." Someone says they want highlights but describes something else entirely. Someone says "that's a bit far for me" but what they really mean is they don't see why it's worth the drive. If you can read what people actually mean and move the conversation forward without being told what to say next, you'll do well here.



If you need to be spoon-fed a script for every situation, this won't work.



THIS IS A SALES ROLE. YOU NEED AT LEAST 6 MONTHS OF EXPERIENCE

PERSUADING PEOPLE AND MOVING THEM TOWARD A BOOKED APPOINTMENT

OR A SALE.



OTE: $1,250–$2,000/month (base $900–$1,000 + uncapped performance bonuses).

13th month pay included — paid every December, on top of your base. Not baked in. Not restructured. A full extra month of base pay, added on top.



---



ABOUT THE COMPANY



You'll be employed by Midnight Siren, a growth and client acquisition company that operates and supports beauty service businesses. Your day-to-day work focuses on a family-owned, color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California that has served the Inland Empire for over 21 years.



The salon has 4.9 stars on Google with 200+ reviews and a stylist team with 75+ combined years of experience. The business is real, established, and respected in its market.



You'll work directly under Ethan, the founder of Midnight Siren — no middle managers, no agency layers between you and the person making decisions. The Midnight Siren team is small and tightly focused. The stylists at salon handle the in-salon experience; you and Ethan handle everything that gets a client booked.



A note on team structure: you will be the only appointment setter on the team. Your day-to-day working relationship is directly with Ethan. There are no peer-level coworkers, no team chat with other appointment setters, no group energy to feed off. If you thrive with autonomy, clear systems, and a direct manager relationship, this works well. If you need a team environment or peer social dynamic to stay motivated, this will feel isolating over time.



We're in an active scaling phase. Core processes exist and are being refined. They don't change daily, but they evolve as we learn. If you like improving systems alongside a team, you'll fit. If you want a fully crystallized corporate environment where nothing ever shifts, you won't.



---



WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BE DOING



This is a front-line revenue role, not customer support.



Daily:



- Call new
/Instagram ad leads within minutes of opt-in (speed matters — you'll have task notifications throughout the day)

- Run our call script for the structured parts of the call, and use our frameworks + your own judgment for discovery and objection handling. The script covers the greeting, the offer, pricing, and the booking ask. Discovery can't be fully scripted — clients say what they say, and you'll need to adapt in real time.

- Respond to inbound SMS,
 
, and Instagram DMs that get escalated to a human when our AI can't handle them

- Collect cards on file via secure link (never over the phone), book appointments, reschedule, and cancel

- Call no-shows to get them back on the calendar

- Coordinate with stylists about client requests and scheduling needs

- Create follow-up tasks in HighLevel (our CRM)

- Submit a brief end-of-day report with your numbers



Weekly:



- One coaching/review call with Ethan (~30–45 min)

- Async coaching via Loom video reviews on your live call recordings between meetings

- Review your KPIs, own your numbers, and bring data-backed ideas to improve them



During training (first 2–4 weeks):



We'll meet daily for live coaching to get you fully ramped before transitioning to the weekly + async cadence.



---



A WORD ON THE CALL SCRIPT (READ CAREFULLY)



We use a script. We also need you to think.



Where the script is fixed: the greeting, how we introduce the salon, how we present the offer, how we state pricing, the booking ask, and our core objection responses. These are tested and they work. You run them as written. Your tone, warmth, and pacing are what make them sound human — not changing the words.



Where the script can't help you: everything a real client throws at you. A vague text with no context. A client describing a service using the wrong name. Someone who's hesitant but won't say why. Someone who asks about price before you've figured out what they actually want. There is no script for these. There's a framework, and there's your judgment.



This is the part people underestimate. A big chunk of this job is not reciting — it's listening to what someone actually means and figuring out the next move in seconds, while they're on the phone with you.



Scripts do change here, but only based on data. If you bring an idea for a better line, we'll A/B test it. If it wins, it becomes the script. What we don't do is let setters freelance changes on the fly, because then we can't measure what works.



If you want to be told exactly what to say in every situation, this role will frustrate you. If you like having strong structure AND room to think, you'll do well.



---



SCHEDULE (PACIFIC TIME — GRAVEYARD SHIFT IN PHILIPPINES)



All schedule references in this post are in US Pacific Time. Because PH is 15-16 hours ahead of California, each shift starts late at night your time and ends the following morning.

- US workdays: Monday through Friday

- US days off: Saturday and Sunday

- Hours per day: 8 hours of work + 1 hour of break (30 min lunch + 2× 15 min breaks, or 30 min lunch + 1× 30 min break — your call)

- Pacific Time (US): 7:45 AM – 4:45 PM PST



Philippine Time during US Standard Time (roughly November through mid-March):



Shift runs 11:45 PM – 8:45 AM PHT

- A US Monday shift = late Monday night through Tuesday morning your time

- A US Friday shift = late Friday night through Saturday morning your time

- Your days off in PH local time: Sunday and Monday (until your shift starts late Monday night)



Philippine Time during US Daylight Savings Time (roughly mid-March through early November):



- Shift runs 10:45 PM – 7:45 AM PHT

- Same day-shift logic as above — shift starts the previous calendar evening in PH



This schedule is FIXED. It's based on data showing when our booking demand peaks. If you need flexible hours, rotating shifts, or plan to hold another job during these times, this role is not a fit.

Please re-read this section carefully and make sure BOTH the standard-time and daylight-savings schedules work for you long-term before applying. The 1-hour shift twice a year is non-negotiable — it follows US business hours. Please make sure BOTH schedules work for you long-term before applying.



---



COMPENSATION



Base pay:



$900–$1,000/month (depending on experience), paid via Wise on the 1st and 15th of every month.



13TH MONTH PAY included — paid every December on top of your regular base, not restructured into it. Prorated in your first year if you start mid-year. Total annualized base compensation including 13th month: $11,700–$13,000.



Performance bonuses (uncapped, paid monthly):



- $3 per new client showed appointment

- $2 per existing client showed appointment

- $1 per rebooking confirmation (low-effort confirmation calls for clients who already booked through the salon)



Tiered cumulative threshold bonuses (paid monthly):



- +$75 at 90 showed appointments/month

- +$150 at 120 showed appointments/month

- +$350 at 150 showed appointments/month



Worked examples:



Baseline performer — 90 showed appointments/month:

- Base: $950 (midpoint)

- Performance: ~$225 (avg $2.50/show × 90)

- Threshold bonus: $75

- Total: ~$1,250/month



Solid performer — 120 showed appointments/month:

- Base: $950

- Performance: ~$300 (avg $2.50/show × 120)

- Threshold bonus: $225 ($75 + $150)

- Total: ~$1,475/month



Top performer — 150 showed appointments/month (90% show rate on ~167 booked):

- Base: $1,000

- Performance: $450 ($3×90 new + $2×20 existing + $1×40 rebooking)

- Threshold bonuses: $575 ($75 + $150 + $350)

- Total: ~$2,025/month



This is a PERFORMANCE-PAY ROLE. 30–50% of your monthly income should be earned through bonuses. The base is intentionally modest. If you want a high guaranteed salary with low expectations, this is not the role.



---



OTHER BENEFITS



1. Annual performance-based raise after your first year

2. 14 days of PTO per year, single bucket, available after 90-day probation (use for vacation, holidays, sickness — your call). For planned multi-day time off, give us at least 1 week's notice so we can plan coverage. Emergencies are understood — just communicate as soon as you can.

3. 90-day initial probation period. Pay is NOT REDUCED during probation.



To confirm you have read this post in full, include the word BURGUNDY in your answer to the final question on the application form



---



TARGET KPIs



- Lead to Booking Rate: 25%+

- Show Rate: 90%+

- Bookings per day: 4–9

- Showed appointments per month: 100–160

- Daily volume: Finish all assigned tasks each day. We supply ~17–25 leads per day plus follow-ups, no-shows, reactivations, and rebooking confirmations. HIGH CALL VOLUME (150–250 CALLS/DAY) IS NORMAL AND NON-NEGOTIABLE. If that sounds overwhelming instead of energizing, this is not a fit.



---



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



Background:



- Female candidates tend to perform best with our 35–65 female clientele, so we especially encourage strong female applicants — but the role is open to all genders.

- Bilingual (English + Spanish) is a plus but not required.



Non-negotiable skills:



The five that matter most — these are what we screen hardest for:



- Real-time thinking. You generate a good response in seconds, not minutes. Under pressure, with no script in front of you. This is the single biggest predictor of success in this role.

- Inferential listening. You hear what someone means, not just what they said. A client says "I need to talk to my husband first" — she's usually not asking for permission, she's telling you something about price or certainty that she doesn't want to say directly. If you take everything at face value, you'll lose bookings.

- Conversational initiative. You never dead-end a conversation, and you don't give up on a lead that's still alive. A client says "that's kind of far for me" — a weak setter says "no problem, thanks anyway" and loses her. What she's actually telling you is that she doesn't believe the drive is worth it yet. That's not a rejection, it's an assumption you haven't disproven. Answering someone's question is only half a response; the other half is the move that keeps things going.

- Rapport building. You can get someone to open up and feel comfortable with you fast. This is the biggest factor in whether someone books. These are emotional decisions, not logical ones. You don't need American cultural references — you need to make people feel heard, understood, and safe.

- Diagnostic reframing. You can say someone's problem back to them more clearly than they said it. When you do that, people assume you have the solution. It's the fastest way to build trust that exists.



Everything else:



- ADVANCED ENGLISH WITH MINIMAL ACCENT. An American listener should not need to strain to understand you. If we have to focus to follow what you're saying, that's a disqualifier.

- STRONG SPOKEN COMMUNICATION — CLEAR, CONFIDENT VOICE. YOU DO NOT RAMBLE. YOU ARE NOT SOFT-SPOKEN. If you fill silence with words because dead air makes you nervous, this won't work.

- Typing speed: 40 wpm minimum (60+ strongly preferred). You'll be taking notes and sending texts while talking. You'll submit a typing test screenshot with your application.

- Process discipline. Every call gets dispositioned correctly. Every lead moves through the right cadence. Every opportunity gets marked accurately in the CRM. This isn't optional admin — it's how we measure everything. Great conversations with sloppy process still means we're flying blind.

- Script discipline for the structured parts of the call.

- Natural call control. You can guide a conversation efficiently without talking over clients or letting calls drift. You redirect politely and keep the call outcome-focused.

- Sales experience: 6 months minimum (1 year+ preferred). Job-hopping resumes (multiple roles under 3–6 months each) will be disqualified.

- Comfortable holding the line on policies (rescheduling, deposits, etc.) without weakening the script or over-promising.

- Objection handling — you acknowledge, ask questions to reframe, and guide the client. You don't fire off rebuttals that invoke more resistance.

- CRM literacy. GoHighLevel experience strongly preferred.

- High data accuracy. You enter info correctly the first time. This is a precision role, not a speed-only one.

- Strong working memory and multitasking — you can listen, think, type, recall rules, and follow scripts simultaneously without freezing.

- Emotional steadiness under high-volume periods. Spikes happen. You execute calm under load.



Preferred:



- Familiarity with the salon/beauty industry

- Personal interest in beauty or self-care

- Experience working with older female clientele (35–65)

- Experience with Slack, Slite, Airtable, Claude or ChatGPT (we use AI to streamline daily work — if you can leverage it, you'll move faster)



Mindset (MOST IMPORTANT):



We'd rather hire someone who's a 10 in mindset and 7 in sales skill than the reverse. Here's what we mean:



- Ownership & volume mindset — you take responsibility for outcomes, not tasks. You see high-volume, repetitive work as leverage, not burnout.

- Process discipline — you operate consistently inside defined systems. You let your personality show through tone and warmth, not by changing the words.

- Sales psychology — you understand how to influence through trust, value framing, and subtle urgency. You communicate with intention, not chit-chat.

- Speed bias — you move fast, close loops quickly, and accelerate under pressure instead of slowing down.

- Coachability — you receive feedback without ego and adapt immediately. No defensiveness, no excuses.

- KPI awareness — you understand the numbers behind your role and how your daily actions move them.



---



TECH REQUIREMENTS



Non-negotiable:



- Internet minimum requirements: 50 Mbps download, 10 Mbps upload, ping under 80ms. Stable connection. We will test your speed and audio live from your actual work setup before we hire.

- Backup plan for outages. If your internet or power cuts out mid-shift, you need a real fallback — mobile hotspot, secondary ISP, UPS, co-working space, or some combination. You'll describe your specific backup setup in your application.

- Computer: 8 GB RAM minimum (16+ preferred). Processor: Intel Core i5 or equivalent, 8th generation or newer. SSD preferred. Working laptop or desktop

- Mouse

- Wired headset with boom mic (3.5mm or USB-C). No Bluetooth, no laptop mic, no AirPods.

- Webcam — laptop built-in is fine. You'll be on camera for interviews, training, and coaching calls.

- Quiet, dedicated workspace. No roosters, no karaoke neighbors, no babies crying, no traffic, no dogs barking during calls. We will hear it on the call, and so will our clients.



Preferred:



- Second monitor

- You already own a headset that meets the requirements above (we'll provide one if you don't, but having your own helps you start faster)



---



DO NOT APPLY IF:



- You struggle to think quickly and respond in real time. If you need a moment to figure out what to say, this role will be painful. Clients don't wait.

- You need the client to lead the conversation. If you're comfortable answering questions but not steering, this isn't it.

- You can't hold a conversation without a script telling you what to say next.

- You type slowly. Under 40 wpm means you'll fall behind on notes and texts while you're talking.

- You have less than 6 months of experience persuading people, handling objections, and closing toward a booked appointment or sale.

- Your spoken English is hard to understand on the phone — this is a phone role first and the single biggest dealbreaker

- You're juggling multiple clients or planning to freelance on the side. THIS MUST BE YOUR ONLY JOB. We track performance closely and will discover this fast.

- You want a high guaranteed salary with low performance pressure

- You don't like high call volume or you find scripts "suffocating"

- You see remote work as "work whenever you feel like it"

- You can't sustain a graveyard shift long-term

- You're looking for a short-term gig — we expect a minimum 12-month commitment after probation



---



HIRING PROCESS



1. Application via Tally form (link below) — includes voice recording, Loom video, internet speed screenshot, backup plan description, and a few short written questions

2. 20-minute pre-screen call with our hiring partner

3. First-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — includes live roleplay

4. Second-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — final fit + offer discussion

5. Offer — targeting hires between August 10 – August 20

6. Paid training begins immediately after offer acceptance



---



HOW TO APPLY



Submit your application through this Tally form: | 
 |



IMPORTANT: There is a confirmation requirement embedded in this post. Applications that miss it will be skipped regardless of experience.



The form will ask for:



- A screenshot of your typing test results (
)

- A screenshot of your internet speedtest (speedtest.net)

- A screenshot of your computer specs (RAM and processor)

- A description of your backup plan for power/internet outages

- A few short questions to gauge fit

- A short voice recording (Vocaroo or similar)

- A short Loom video introducing yourself



Applications submitted via direct messages on OnlineJobs.ph will NOT be reviewed. Use the Tally form.



---



Looking forward to meeting the right person.



Ethan

Founder, Midnight Siren



---



Full-Time | Long-Term | Remote | Pacific Time (Graveyard Shift in PH)

title: Creative Writing, Short Stories for Psychology Game
description:
Hi there, I'm Helen, and I'm the founder of a company called Trove. (www.trove.is).



Trove is a free choose your own adventure game x personality quiz that you play everyday. Over time, it builds up to a stronger and more honest profile of who someone is, beyond what resumes and other profiles can share about a person today. My goal here is a more authentic world... and it starts with play!



I'm looking for a writer to help with crafting short and medium length stories for Trove. 



The stories right now are roughly 70% human-authored with the remainder being 30% AI-assisted writing (because players can do whatever they want, so we use AI to be able to generate adaptable pages. So we'll be using your core stories, characters, plot lines, while using AI to allow for adaptability. 



Your responsibilities will include ideating plotlines (with an eye for understanding also what we can learn from someone based on what they do within your stories), writing the stories in our proprietary authoring system as well as testing/editing them to get them ready for users to play. 



For reference, each short story currently takes me roughly 3-5 hours to ideate, test, write and consider ready for publishing. I'd expect you to be better + faster than me... but I might also want to transition us into writing longer stories. So for now I'd say I expect you to write at least 2-3 playable short stories per week. 



We'll work mainly off of 
 on pre-set times you're available, on a daily basis ideally. I'm happy to figure out a schedule that works for both of us.



In terms of working with me, I'm someone who is reasonably relaxed and not micro-manage-y, but very detail-oriented. Well I guess I can be micro-manage-y, but that only happens if I don't trust you and trust is the hallmark of any good collaboration. I am absolutely a perfectionist though. To learn more about me, you can find some of our other job posts on the official website and that should give you a sense of the kind of company I'm building.

title: Facebook Ads D2C Video Editor
description:
We're looking for a video editor who understands one thing clearly:



A good ad doesn't just look nice. It stops the scroll, holds attention, builds desire, and gets people to take action.



We're a fast-growing e-commerce brand creating products in the health and wellness niche, and paid social is one of our main growth channels. That means video creative is not just "content" for us, it's one of the biggest drivers of the business.



We're looking for an editor who can help us create high-performing video ads for
, Instagram and other paid channels.



This role is ideal for someone who understands direct-response editing, UG-style ads, fast testing, strong hooks, emotional storytelling, and conversion-focused creative.



— WHAT YOU'LL BE EDITING —



You'll be working on video ads designed specifically for e-commerce performance, including:

-
 and Instagram ads: scroll-stopping videos built to grab attention quickly and drive purchases

- AI voiceover ads: A simple combination of voiceover and b-rolls, chosen carefully and enhanced with copy, graphic and sound effects, zooms, transitions, etc.

education and direct-response structure

- UGC-style ad creatives: native-feeling videos that look organic, believable, and platform-friendly

- Product demonstration videos: clear, benefit-driven edits that show the product in action

- Customer testimonial ads: emotional, trust-building edits using reviews, before/after moments, and social proof

- Creative variations for testing: different hooks, openings, captions, CTAs, angles, pacing, and structures



— WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR —



We're not looking for a "cinematic" editor who only cares about pretty visuals.

We're looking for someone who understands how ads work.



You should know how to edit videos that:

- Stop people in the first 1-3 seconds

- Make the problem feel real and urgent

- Show the product clearly and persuasively

- Use captions, cuts, zooms, overlays, and b-roll to maintain attention

- Feel native to
, Instagram, and TikTok

- Communicate benefits quickly and clearly

- Build trust using reviews, testimonials, and social proof

- Guide the viewer toward a click or purchase



You should be able to take a script, raw footage, UGC clips, product shots, reviews, references, and creative notes... then turn them into a polished ad ready for testing.



— THE KIND OF EDITOR WHO WILL THRIVE HERE —



You'll be a strong fit if you:

- Have experience editing video ads for e-commerce brands

- Understand direct-response marketing and paid social creative

- Can create multiple ad variations quickly

- Know how to follow references without copying them blindly

- Have a good instinct for hooks, pacing, retention, and emotional flow

- Can make simple footage feel compelling and conversion-focused

- Are comfortable receiving feedback and iterating fast

- Care about whether your videos actually perform, not just whether they look good



We care about creative that sells. That doesn't mean ugly or low-quality. It means every editing choice should support the message, the emotion, and the conversion.



— SKILLS & EXPERIENCE —



Ideally, you have experience with:

- Meta/Facebook ad creatives

- Short-form paid social videos

- ??Long-form VSLs or sales videos

- Captioning, motion graphics, overlays, b-roll, sound design, and pacing

- Premiere Pro, After Effects, CapCut, DaVinci, or similar tools



Bonus if you've worked with in the health and wellness niche.



— WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING DAY TO DAY —



- Editing new ad creatives from scripts, footage, UGC clips, and references

- Creating variations of winning ads for further testing

- Improving hooks, pacing, captions, visuals, and CTAs

- Adapting creatives for different platforms and aspect ratios

- Collaborating with the marketing and creative team to improve performance

- Using feedback from ad results to make stronger iterations



— WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU —



- Competitive compensation based on experience

- Performance-based bonuses for strong creatives

- The opportunity to work on ads that directly drive revenue

- Clear creative direction and fast feedback

- Long-term growth with a brand aiming to scale aggressively

title: Junior Marketing Virtual Assistant | Motivated & Detail-Oriented - US Hours
description:
Hello, we’re looking to hire a full-time Junior Marketing Virtual Assistant to support our agency with the day-to-day tasks that keep our clients’ marketing running smoothly.



We help ecommerce brands grow through paid ads, creative strategy, and better marketing systems.



We do not expect you to already know everything.



We’re open to someone who is still early in their career and may be a little raw. What matters much more to us is that you’re motivated, reliable, detail-oriented, and genuinely willing to learn.



You’ll work alongside our team and learn by doing. You’ll help with research, creative coordination, reporting, organization, and general marketing support.



At first, you’ll receive more guidance. As you learn our systems and prove yourself, we’ll expect you to become more independent and take ownership of more tasks.



For the right person, this can be an opportunity to learn ecommerce marketing from inside an agency and eventually grow into a more specialized marketing or creative role.



We’re looking for someone with potential, not someone who already has everything figured out.



WHAT THIS ROLE ACTUALLY DOES



You’ll support the team across a mix of marketing and admin tasks.



You won’t be expected to own client accounts or make major marketing decisions on day one.



You’ll learn by helping the team, following instructions carefully, asking good questions, and gradually taking on more responsibility.



• Support the team with day-to-day marketing tasks across client accounts

• Research competitors, products, brands, and the Meta/Facebook Ad Library

• Organize creative assets, files, links, and documentation

• Help prepare creative briefs and gather product information

• Assist with pulling performance data and creating simple reports

• Coordinate tasks between designers, strategists, and other team members

• Keep project management tools and trackers up to date

• Upload, schedule, and organize ads and content

• Help with basic edits, formatting, and content organization

• Follow up on tasks and make sure things don’t get forgotten

• Handle general admin and marketing support when needed

• Take feedback from the team and apply it to your next task



WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE



We don’t expect perfection from day one.



We do expect effort, improvement, and attention to detail.



• You complete tasks accurately and on time

• You follow instructions carefully

• Your files, assets, and trackers stay organized

• Your research is thorough and useful

• You ask questions when you’re genuinely stuck instead of guessing

• You learn from feedback and avoid repeating the same mistakes

• You double-check your work before submitting it

• You communicate clearly and keep the team updated

• You become more independent as you learn

• Over time, you start taking ownership of recurring tasks



WHAT WE CARE MOST ABOUT



• Motivation - You genuinely want to learn, improve, and become good at what you do.

• Attention to detail - You notice small things. Names, numbers, offers, spelling, links, and formatting matter.

• Willingness to learn - You don’t need to know everything, but you need to be teachable and willing to figure things out.

• Reliability - If you say you’ll do something, we should be able to trust that it gets done.

• Organization - You keep tasks, files, and information organized and easy to find.

• Resourcefulness - Before immediately asking someone else, you’re willing to research, use Google or AI, and try to find an answer.

• Communication - You respond during working hours and tell us early if you’re stuck or falling behind.

• Ownership - Even as a junior, you care about whether the work is actually done correctly.



• Interest in marketing - You don’t need deep marketing knowledge yet, but you should genuinely want to learn how ecommerce brands grow online.



SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE



Previous agency experience is not required.



You also don’t need years of marketing experience.



We’re happy to consider someone early in their career if they show strong potential.



Relevant experience could include:



• Marketing

• Ecommerce

• Social media

• Content creation

• Virtual assistance

• Admin support

• Data entry

• Customer service

• Digital marketing

• Personal projects or self-taught marketing experience



You may already know some of these tools, or simply be willing to learn them:



• Google Sheets

• Notion

• Canva

• Meta Ads Library

• Meta Ads Manager

• ChatGPT

• Claude

• Asana, ClickUp, or similar project management tools

• Other research, organization, and AI tools



You do not need experience with every tool listed above.



If you’ve never used some of them before, that’s completely fine. We care more about how quickly you can learn.



Bonus if you have:



• Some experience with ecommerce or marketing

• Familiarity with Meta/Facebook ads

• Basic spreadsheet or reporting experience

• Experience organizing content or creative assets

• Experience working remotely with a team



WHO THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR



This role is probably not a fit if you:



• Don’t pay attention to details

• Regularly miss deadlines

• Need to be reminded repeatedly about the same tasks

• Don’t like researching or figuring things out

• Get defensive when receiving feedback

• Repeat the same mistakes without improving

• Have no interest in ecommerce or marketing

• Aren’t comfortable learning new tools

• Only want a short-term freelance job

• Want a role where you can do the same simple tasks forever without taking on more responsibility



We are happy to teach someone who doesn’t know something yet.



We are much less concerned with what you know today than how quickly you learn once you’re shown.



SCHEDULE



Full-time, 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday.



Remote.



You should be able to communicate consistently during working hours and work well with an international team.



COMPENSATION



30,000 PHP/month



There is room to grow over time as your skills, reliability, and responsibilities increase.



QUESTIONS



1. What experience do you have with marketing, ecommerce, admin support, virtual assistance, or similar work? It’s okay if your experience is limited.

2. How do you stay organized when you have several tasks to complete?

3. Tell us about something you taught yourself recently. What did you do when you didn’t know how to do it?

4. What tools are you currently comfortable using? Rate your experience with each from 1 to 10.

5. Tell us about a time you made a mistake at work or school. What did you do after you noticed it?



IMPORTANT



To apply, start your application message with the word Detail on the first line.



Applications that do not follow this instruction will not be reviewed.



TRIAL TASK



Shortlisted applicants may be asked to complete 1 small paid trial task.



The task will help us understand how you research, organize information, follow instructions, and pay attention to details.



We aren’t expecting expert-level marketing knowledge.



We want to see how you think, how carefully you work, and how willing you are to figure things out.



The task won’t be long or time-consuming.



GROWTH PATH



First 30 days



• Learn our systems, tools, and processes

• Understand how our team works

• Learn the basics of ecommerce marketing

• Complete simple recurring tasks accurately

• Keep files and trackers organized

• Get comfortable asking questions and receiving feedback

• Become reliable with day-to-day support



After 60 to 90 days



• Complete more tasks without step-by-step guidance

• Take ownership of recurring responsibilities

• Handle research and basic reporting more independently

• Understand our clients and their marketing better

• Start supporting more parts of the marketing process

• Identify areas where you’re especially strong



Longer term



For someone who keeps learning and performing well, the path could look like:



Junior Marketing VA → Marketing VA → Marketing Specialist → Creative Strategist / Media Buyer



The exact path depends on your strengths and what you become good at.



We don’t promise promotions or specific timelines. Growth comes with increased skill, reliability, ownership, and responsibility.



If you’re early in your career but motivated, curious, detail-oriented, and hungry to learn, we’d love to hear from you.



You don’t need to come in knowing everything.



You do need to come in ready to learn.

title: Customer Success Manager, Marketing

You will work directly with clients to understand their goals, develop realistic marketing strategies, present campaign recommendations, monitor performance, and coordinate with internal creative and fulfillment teams to ensure campaigns are executed effectively.



This role is focused specifically on paid advertising and digital marketing strategy and will work alongside the Fulfillment team, who owns the overall client relationship and onboarding process.

Key Responsibilities



Campaign Strategy & Management: Develop, launch, manage, and optimize paid advertising campaigns based on client goals, audience, budget, and historical performance.



Performance & Budget Monitoring: Track campaign metrics and spend to identify issues, opportunities, and trends, and take corrective action as needed.



Optimization & Scaling: Make data-driven adjustments to improve lead generation, conversion performance, and efficiency while identifying opportunities to scale.



Digital Marketing Strategy: Develop recommendations across offers, landing pages, creative, targeting, funnels, and other digital marketing components that impact campaign performance.

title: Short-Form Video Editor — Personal Brand, Instagram Reels (Part-Time)
description:
ABOUT ME



I run an ecommerce business and I post about it on Instagram — building the company, training and the gym, and life in Barcelona. The point of the page is to show people what's actually possible when you commit to something, and to be a real example of it rather than a highlight reel.



My Instagram handle is jaspar_s — look me up before you apply, so you know what you'd be working on.



I started a few months ago and the account is at around 5,000 followers and growing. I film everything myself, every day. The problem is that I no longer have the time to edit it, and half of what I shoot never gets posted. That's the job.



THE WORK



- I drop raw footage into a shared Google Drive folder — clips from my day, gym sessions, and takes of me talking to camera

- You cut them into finished vertical videos for Instagram Reels

- You choose the music and cut to it

- You add captions and on-screen text where it actually helps, not everywhere

- You find the odd extra shot when a video needs one — a scene-setter to open on, a transition

- You drop the finished MP4s back into the same folder

- Around 4-6 videos a week to start, more as we get into a rhythm



To be clear about what this is not: you don't manage my Instagram, you don't post, you don't reply to comments, and you don't need a content strategy. I do all of that. You edit.



THREE KINDS OF VIDEO YOU'LL BE CUTTING



1. Me talking to camera — about business, ecommerce, discipline, training. Long rambling takes that need to become 30-45 tight seconds. Cutting the dead air without it feeling choppy is the skill here.



2. Day in the life — b-roll of the day: working, travelling, walking through the city, coffee, gym, whatever I shot. Little or no dialogue. This one lives or dies on pacing and music.



3. Training and gym — rhythm and energy, music-led.



YOU'RE A GREAT FIT IF YOU



- Edit short-form vertical content regularly, and your portfolio shows it

- Have genuine taste in music and know how to cut on the beat — this is the single thing I care most about

- Can take a four-minute talking take and make it 40 seconds that hold attention

- Bring your own ideas. I'll give you footage and a direction, not a shot list. If you see a better way to build the video, I want you to take it.

- Can hold a consistent look week after week, so the page has a style instead of looking like ten different editors

- Turn a video around in 24-48 hours

- Write clear, natural English and are easy to reach

- Are reliable. Consistency beats brilliance here — I'd rather have good videos every week than great ones sometimes.



NICE TO HAVE



- You actually watch this kind of content — fitness, business, lifestyle creators — and have opinions about who's good

- Comfortable in CapCut, Premiere Pro or After Effects

- You can do a clean auto-caption pass and style it well

- You know where to find good stock b-roll when a video needs a shot I didn't film

- Some sense of colour grading — I want the videos to feel warm and cinematic, not flat phone footage



COMPENSATION



Competitive, based on experience — we'll discuss it on the call. Part-time to start, and I'd rather build this into something long-term with one person than rotate through freelancers.



TO APPLY — READ THIS PART CAREFULLY



There's a short test, and I only read applications that include it. I know that's real work. I'd rather see one video you cut than a list of software you own.



Step 1 — Put the word BARCELONA at the very top of your application, so I know you read this.



Step 2 — Get the footage. OnlineJobs removes links from job posts, so you'll have to type this one in yourself. Go to drive dot google dot com and add this to the end of the address:



/drive/folders/1XBR6FxSO5MasxMwHWYHkXYm7kibUVOuG



Inside you'll find the raw clips and a short brief. Read the brief first — it has the two videos I'm using as inspiration.



Step 3 — Cut one video. One finished Instagram Reel from that footage. Vertical, 1080 x 1920, between 20 and 45 seconds, with music.



You don't have to use every clip — use what works. You're also welcome to add an outside shot if the video needs one, like something to open on. Beyond that the creative call is yours, and that's the point of the test: I want to see your ideas, not just your software skills.



Step 4 — Send me:



- The finished video as an MP4

- Two or three sentences on why you cut it that way: the track you chose and why, what you left out, and which shots (if any) aren't from my footage

- A link to your portfolio or recent short-form work

- How long it took you



Send it as one link — Google Drive, Dropbox or WeTransfer.



Applications without the video are not read. If something in the brief is unclear, ask me before you start — a question costs nothing.

title: Direct Response Copywriter for DTC eCommerce supplements brand
description:
Yes. The problem is that your current post is broad enough that journalists, general copywriters, and content writers can all reasonably apply.



You need to make the positioning much narrower: DTC/eCommerce direct response only, preferably people who have actually worked on paid traffic for health, beauty, wellness, fashion, or similar consumer products.



I would rewrite it like this:



Direct Response Copywriter for DTC eCommerce Brands



We are looking for a Direct Response Copywriter who is already in the eCommerce game.



This is NOT a journalism, content writing, SEO, blogging, or general copywriting position.



We work with DTC/eCommerce brands and dropshipping businesses, and we need someone who understands how to take a product from research → angle → advertorial/listicle → Meta ads → Shopify page → conversion.



You should already understand how eCommerce brands acquire customers through Meta/Facebook advertising and direct response funnels.



The Ideal Candidate



You have already worked with:



• DTC/eCommerce brands

• Dropshipping brands

• Health & wellness products

• Beauty/skincare products

• Women’s health products

• Supplements or consumer health products

• Fashion or lifestyle products



You understand direct response copywriting, not just “good writing.”



You know how to find:



• Winning angles

• Customer pain points

• Emotional triggers

• Objections

• Awareness levels

• Unique mechanisms

• Market sophistication

• Big ideas

• Hooks

• Product benefits

• Customer desires



And most importantly, you understand how these elements connect to paid traffic and conversions.



What You Will Do



You will primarily work on:



• Advertorials

• Listicles

• Pre sell pages

• Meta/Facebook ad copy

• Hooks and creative angles

• Product positioning

• Customer research

• Competitor research

• Landing page copy

• Shopify page building and formatting



You should be comfortable taking a product and building the entire direct response messaging angle around it, rather than simply being given every idea and asked to write it.



You MUST Have eCommerce Experience



We are specifically looking for someone who has already worked with brands, dropshippers, agencies, or eCommerce businesses.



If your experience is primarily:



Journalism

Blog writing

SEO content

Academic writing

Generic website copy

Social media content



this position is probably not for you.



We want someone who has actually worked on products being sold online through paid traffic.



Proof of Experience Is Required



Please send:



1. The eCommerce brands you have worked with

2. The niches/products you worked on

3. Your best 2 to 3 advertorials or listicles

4. Examples of Meta/Facebook ads you personally wrote

5. Examples of Shopify landing pages or presell pages you built

6. Any results you can share such as ROAS, CPA, CTR, conversion rate, revenue, or winning campaigns

7. Explain exactly what YOU did on each project



We are much more interested in real work and real results than a beautiful portfolio.



If you have worked on a campaign that spent significant money and your copy contributed to its success, tell us about it.



Shopify Experience



You should be comfortable building the actual pages inside Shopify.



We don’t want someone who only sends a Google Doc with copy and waits for someone else to build everything.



You should be able to take your copy and turn it into a properly structured advertorial/listicle/presell page inside Shopify.



Part Time To Start



We are looking to start part time, with the possibility of moving into a larger/full time role if the collaboration works well.



Compensation will depend on your experience and proven results.



There is potential for a long term position working across multiple eCommerce brands.



IMPORTANT: Start Your Application Correctly



At the very beginning of your application, write:



I AM ALREADY IN ECOMMERCE



Then answer these questions:



1. What eCommerce/DTC brands have you worked with?



2. What niches have you worked in?



3. What was your role?



4. What was the approximate monthly ad spend of the brands/campaigns you worked on?



5. Give us one example of a piece of copy you wrote that performed well and explain why you think it worked.



6. Send your 2 best advertorial/listicle examples.



7. Send your best Meta ad examples.



8. What is your experience building pages in Shopify?



Generic applications will not be considered.



We are looking for someone who already understands DTC direct response and has been in the game.

About Our Company

We are an established, high-volume commercial logistics and paper distribution company based in California, USA, managing a steady annual freight spend of over $350,000. We operate a fast-paced warehouse environment and are completely restructuring our back-office logistics tracking into a highly optimized digital dashboard.

We do not hire temporary freelancers or multi-client virtual assistants. We are looking for an elite, career-minded logistics professional to join our team long-term. You will enter a highly secure, premium compensation structure designed for absolute career longevity.

------------------------------

Core Responsibilities



* Freight Procurement & Spot-Market Squeezing: Take complete ownership of our primary shipping lanes. You must run a strict "three-quote rule" on every load, aggressively audit carrier invoices, and utilize digital spot boards to systematically strip hidden broker markups.

* Compliance & Custom Documentation: Independently manage, verify, and input complex international customs paperwork, including USMCA Certificates of Origin, Spanish Commercial Invoices, and standard alphanumeric Bills of Lading (BOL).

* Traffic Coordination & Live Tracking: Schedule carrier dock appointments via digital portals. Maintain a strict 0% data entry error rate, and broadcast real-time bay commands and tracking data directly onto our live warehouse wall display monitor via a continuous video connection.

* Team Communication: Work directly as an administrative partner to our local, on-site Bilingual Forklift Lead Supervisor in California, coordinating trailer staging data via direct messaging systems.



------------------------------

Non-Negotiable Mandatory Requirements

1. Absolute Employment Exclusivity (Moonlighting Policy)



* Single-Client Only: This role demands your complete professional focus. You are strictly prohibited from holding any other part-time jobs, freelance gigs, or secondary clients while employed with us.

* Background Checks: We perform random, periodic network audits and require full transparency. Discovery of secondary employment or moonlighting will result in immediate termination without pay.



2. Live Warehouse Video Stream Requirement



* Continuous Visual Presence: Because you are driving the live data wall display monitor inside our physical California facility, you are required to maintain an active, high-definition webcam feed directly to our warehouse floor for the entirety of your shift.

* Operational Purpose: This is not for micromanagement; your feed allows our on-site Forklift Supervisors to visually sync with you on incoming trailer staging data and immediate dock scheduling adjustments.

* Workspace Setup: You must have a clean, quiet, well-lit, and professional home office space free of background noise, family disruptions, or ambient clutter.



3. Grid & Geographic Restriction

To protect our live data stream from regional power failure, you must permanently reside in one of the following low-blackout zones:



* Davao City (Highly preferred due to superior grid reserves and placement outside the typhoon belt).

* Metro Manila Premium Districts (Bonifacio Global City, Makati, or Ortigas only).

* Applicants residing in the Visayas region (Cebu, Dumaguete, Iloilo) or rural provinces will be automatically disqualified.



4. Hardware & Infrastructure Security

You must possess a bulletproof remote setup, including:



* An active, high-speed Starlink terminal connection.

* A secondary, independent 5G or fiber internet backup line with automated failover.

* A dedicated gas inverter generator or heavy-duty solar battery station (e.g., EcoFlow) hooked to an active UPS power supply.



5. Verified Professional Experience



* Minimum 5 to 8+ years of professional corporate experience working inside a U.S. domestic freight brokerage, container dispatch hub, or international supply chain analysis office.

* Absolute, expert-level command of U.S. spot-market digital load boards (such as DAT, Truckstop, etc.), carrier API portals, and digital freight tracking spreadsheets.

* Flawless, professional, executive-level spoken and written English.



------------------------------

 What We Offer



* Top-of-Market Fixed Payout: A premium flat salary of $3,466.00 USD per month, paid safely and on time every single week via Wise [Glassdoor].

* Guaranteed Stability: A baseline guarantee of 40 hours of paid work every single week. We provide a stable career relationship working straight for the business owner with zero agency middlemen or platform fees.

* Lighter Workflow Efficiency: While you are paid for a full 40-hour week to guarantee your dedication, a highly proficient specialist who optimizes their dashboard can easily complete the core daily data processing loop in 4 to 6 hours of high-speed execution, leaving your remaining shift open for strategic lane analysis.



------------------------------

How to Apply (Mandatory Steps)

To be considered, reply with the subject line: "Exclusive Logistics Specialist - [Your City: Davao or Manila]" and include:



   1. Mandatory Voice Recording: Provide a link to a 1-to-2 minute audio recording of yourself (using a free tool like Loom, Vocaroo, or Google Drive). In the recording, state your name and summarize your professional corporate U.S. freight and logistics experience. Applications missing this audio recording will be automatically deleted without review.

   2. Your updated resume detailing your U.S. freight experience.
